{{Quote|Lord Vader, this is an unexpected pleasure. We are honored by your presence.''"<br />"''You may dispense with the pleasantries, Commander. I'm here to put you back on schedule.|Tiaan Jerjerrod receives Darth Vader aboard the second Death Star|audio=ImHereToPutYouBackOnSchedule.flac|<ref name="ROTJ" />}}
'''Tiaan Jerjerrod''' {{Pronounced|dʒærˈdʒærrʌd}} was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Imperial officer/Legends|Imperial officer]] who hailed from a wealthy family from the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core World]] of [[Tinnel IV/Legends|Tinnel IV]]. Considered unambitious yet efficient by his peers, Jerjerrod worked as a desk [[General/Legends|general]] in the [[Imperial Supply Corps]] before becoming [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] of the [[Quanta sector/Legends|Quanta sector]] by [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]]. His [[Sector/Legends|sector]] operations were based in a family estate in [[Val Denn/Legends|Val Denn]], the capital city of Tinnel IV. By [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], Jerjerrod had been assigned to oversee the construction of the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]] above the [[Endor/Legends|forest moon]] of [[Endor (planet)/Legends|Endor]], appointed to that position by [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] himself. To hide the existence of the new [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]], records claimed Jerjerrod had been made [[Director/Legends|Director]] of [[Imperial Energy Systems/Legends|Imperial Energy Systems]] and assigned to oversee the construction of large-scale power generators. Moff Jerjerrod frequently had to brief the [[Supreme Commander (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Supreme Commander]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], on the station's construction; on one occasion, he traveled to the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|Star Dreadnought]] [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']] during the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] [[occupation of Bespin]] to report to the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor's]] [[Sith apprentice/Legends|lieutenant]].

Whereas the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]] had taken around nineteen years to complete, the construction of the much-larger second Death Star had moved into its final stage of assembly by [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], after approximately two to four years. However, the construction crews had fallen behind schedule; Vader ventured to the [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] to inform Jerjerrod that the issue needed to be rectified. The [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]] announced that his [[Sith Master/Legends|master]] would be arriving to personally oversee the last stage of the Death Star's construction. Jerjerrod informed Vader that his men would double their efforts, as he was afraid of reporting his failure directly to Palpatine. The Moff was among those assembled to greet the Emperor when he arrived.

The [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] had learned of the second Death Star's construction and the Emperor's presence aboard it via the [[Bothan Spynet/Legends|Bothan Spynet]], and they launched an [[Battle of Endor/Legends|attack]] based on false information released by the sovereign himself. When the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]] arrived, they discovered that the [[SLD-26 planetary shield generator/Legends|planetary shield]] protecting the Death Star was still activated and that the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] was situated to prevent the Rebels from escaping. The Emperor had ordered [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Firmus Piett/Legends|Firmus Piett]] not to directly engage the Rebel [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]], a move that confused personnel on both sides. The reason behind this became clear when Palpatine ordered Jerjerrod to fire the Death Star's operational [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]] at the Alliance Fleet; many Rebel [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]] were obliterated. When the Alliance gained the upper hand in the conflict, the Emperor commanded the Moff to fire on the forest moon. Before he could complete his final order, Jerjerrod [[Death/Legends|perished]] when the Death Star was destroyed.

==Biography==
===Moff of the Quanta sector===
[[File:Jerjerrod-Emperor.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Moff Jerjerrod kneels before the Emperor in the Imperial Palace.]]
{{Quote|You're just a Moff, Jerjerrod&mdash;you couldn't possibly have been given any duty of significance.|Bregius Golthan|<ref name="SOTE">''[[Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref>}}
Tiaan Jerjerrod<ref name="Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> was a [[Force-attunement|Force-attuned]]<ref name="CCG card">{{CCG|set=Death Star II Limited|cardname=Moff Jerjerrod}}</ref> [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]]<ref name="ROTJ" /> who hailed from a wealthy family native to<ref name="TOSVC" /> the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core World]]<ref name="Atlas" /> of [[Tinnel IV/Legends|Tinnel IV]]. His [[Jerjerrod (admiral)|grandfather]] had served as an [[Admiral/Legends|admiral]] in the [[Republic Navy/Legends|navy]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]; Admiral Jerjerrod's connections with then-[[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] greatly benefited the Jerjerrod family.<ref name="TOSVC" /> Tiaan Jerjerrod started his [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] career in the [[Imperial Supply Corps]] as a desk officer, and he eventually rose to the [[Military rank/Legends|rank]] of [[General/Legends|General]].<ref name="GG5">''[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi]]''</ref><ref name="Movie Trilogy Sourcebook">''[[The Movie Trilogy Sourcebook]]''</ref> Because he was not ambitious and took great pride in destroying his enemies,<ref name="TOSVC" /> he became a [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] by [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]], commanding his home [[Sector/Legends|sector]], the [[Quanta sector/Legends|Quanta sector]], from a family estate in [[Val Denn/Legends|Val Denn]] on his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of Tinnel IV. His estate included a vault of artwork, several pieces of which were stolen by the master thief "[[Tanda Marelle|Tombat]]." The thefts were investigated by an Imperial investigator named [[Cammel Atarul]].<ref name="AJ6">{{JournalCite|6|Galaxywide NewsNets}}</ref>

Around 1 ABY, Jerjerrod dispatched an encoded transmission stating that a [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] operative had intercepted encrypted documents related to the research initiative known as [[Project Dead Eye]]. The Moff authorized the recipients of the message to eliminate any Rebels involved in the theft, adding that security was being increased for the project and its leader, [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Vacca]]. Moff Jerjerrod concluded his transmission with a personal note, stressing the importance of Project Dead Eye and the need for absolute secrecy&mdash;and that should anything go wrong, the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military's]] [[Supreme Commander (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Supreme Commander]],<ref name="kenner">{{KennerCite|set=Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (toy line)|pack=Darth Vader vs. Prince Xizor|link=soteKxizor-vader.asp}}</ref> [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] himself, would have his head.<ref name="Galaxies">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref> At one point, Jerjerrod was featured in an advertisement for [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards's]] [[All Terrain Scout Transport/Legends|All Terrain Scout Transport]], giving the corporation a thumb's-up.<ref name="Ad">[[:File:KDYAd-SWI86.jpg|Advertisement]] from the back cover of [[Star Wars Insider 86|''Star Wars Insider'' 86]]</ref>

===The second Death Star===
{{Quote|For the next several months our schedule is exceedingly tight, with no tolerance for delay. We must redouble our efforts.|Jerjerrod|<ref name="Therefore I Am">{{StoryCite|story=Therefore I Am: The Tale of IG-88|book=Tales of the Bounty Hunters}}</ref>}}
As early as [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]],<ref name="Choices">''[[Choices of One]]''</ref> the Empire had been in the process of constructing a [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]]<ref name="ROTJ" /> to replace the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|one]] lost in the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> In selecting a lone [[Commander/Legends|commander]] for the new battlestation, [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] Palpatine looked for someone weak and unambitious, not wanting the new [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] to be commanded by a triumvirate of ambitious men<ref name="GG5" /><ref name="Movie Trilogy Sourcebook" /> like [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]], [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Conan Antonio Motti/Legends|Conan Antonio Motti]], and [[High General]] [[Cassio Tagge/Legends|Cassio Tagge]] aboard the first.<ref name="ANH" /> Palpatine chose Jerjerrod for the position.<ref name="GG5" /><ref name="Movie Trilogy Sourcebook" /> Within the [[Emperor's throne room#Imperial Palace|throne room]] of the [[Imperial Palace/Legends|Imperial Palace]] on the Imperial [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] informed the Moff that he would be transferred from Logistics and Supply to his new assignment. Jerjerrod was somewhat upset with the news, and though he was not foolish enough to openly voice his opinion, Palpatine read his mind and informed him that his talents would not go to waste with his new assignment.<ref name="SOTE" />

[[File:MoffJerjerrodGreetsVader.jpg|thumb|right|250px|As overseer of the Death Star project, Jerjerrod was required to report to Darth Vader at times, such as when the Moff traveled to the ''Executor''.]]
To hide the existence of the new battlestation and create a plausible reason for the Moff's reassignment, Imperial records were doctored to indicate that Jerjerrod had been promoted to [[Director/Legends|Director]] of [[Imperial Energy Systems/Legends|Imperial Energy Systems]], a branch of the Imperial [[Ministry of Energy]]. IES was a manufacturer of large-scale power generators that, officially, were used to provide a source of power for refugees; unofficially, the generators were built for use aboard the second Death Star.<ref name="AJ6" /> As Moff Jerjerrod departed the Emperor's throne room after being given his assignment, he was confronted by [[Imperial Advisor/Legends|Imperial advisors]] [[Bregius Golthan]], [[Alec Pradeux]], and [[Kren Blista-Vanee/Legends|Kren Blista-Vanee]], all of whom believed that he was a man of little importance, too insignificant to earn the attention of the Emperor. The Moff responded by giving the fabricated story for his reassignment, informing the [[Advisor/Legends|advisors]] of his new position as head of Imperial Energy Systems. As the trio taunted him about his apparent demotion, Jerjerrod silently told himself that he had essentially been entrusted with overseeing the destruction of the Rebel Alliance.<ref name="SOTE" />

As overseer of the new Death Star, Jerjerrod&mdash;now simply addressed as "[[Commander/Legends|Commander]]"&mdash;was stationed at the battlestation's construction site<ref name="ROTJ" /> in the [[Endor system/Legends|Endor system]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim's]] [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell sector]].<ref name="Atlas" /> He had been given the overall responsibility of organizing the defense of the Death Star's [[SLD-26 planetary shield generator/Legends|planetary shield]] and its [[Endor shield generator bunker|control bunker]] on the [[Endor/Legends|Forest Moon of Endor]]. In this role, he worked worked closely with [[Colonel/Legends|Colonel]] [[Dyer/Legends|Dyer]] and Commander [[Igar/Legends|Igar]] in planning the defenses and assigning personnel.<ref name="FF11">{{FactFile|11|END 7-10|The Battle of Endor}}</ref><ref name="Igar">{{CCG|set=Endor Limited|cardname=Commander Igar}}</ref> Jerjerrod also charged the [[V-series droid supervisor/Legends|V-series droid supervisor]] [[AV-6R7/Legends|AV-6R7]] with overseeing the various [[Labor droid/Legends|labor droids]] that aided in the construction of the battlestation.<ref name="Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref> Moff Jerjerrod traveled to the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|Star Dreadnought]] [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']]<ref name="TOSVC" />&mdash;at the [[Time/Legends|time]] present in the [[Bespin system/Legends|Bespin system]] during the Empire's [[Occupation of Bespin|occupation]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]]<ref name="ESB" />&mdash;to report to [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] Vader on the ongoing construction of the second Death Star.<ref name="TOSVC" /> After Vader [[Duel on Cloud City/Legends|dueled]] with his son, the Rebel commander and aspiring [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], in Cloud City, Jerjerrod greeted the [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] when his [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] landed in the [[Star Dreadnought/Legends|Star Dreadnought's]] [[Hangar/Legends|hangar]] bay.<ref name="ESB" />

====Construction setbacks====
{{Quote|The Emperor is coming here?''"<br />"''That is correct, Commander, and he is most displeased with your apparent lack of progress.''"<br />"''We shall double our efforts!''"<br />"''I hope so, Commander, for your sake. The Emperor is not as forgiving as I am.|Jerjerrod and Vader discuss the Emperor's impending visit to the second Death Star|audio=WeShallDoubleOurEfforts.flac|<ref name="ROTJ" />}}
[[File:Jerjerrods_Task_BotF.png|thumb|left|250px|Vader conveys Palpatine's displeasure to Jerjerrod]]
By [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], the crews responsible for the construction of the second Death Star had become lax in their work.<ref name="ROTJ" /> Because his crews were behind schedule, Commander Jerjerrod had no time to inspect a new [[Computer core/Legends|computer core]] that had arrived for installation aboard the Death Star, instead cursing [[Supervisor/Legends|Supervisor]] [[Gurdun]] for not accompanying the unit to the battlestation as planned. Unbeknownst to the Moff, the rogue [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droid]] and [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[IG-88A/Legends|IG-88A]] had uploaded his consciousness into a duplicate computer core as part of his plot to use the second Death Star as a makeshift "body" from which to initiate his [[Droid Revolution]]. In truth, Gurdun had accompanied the computer core until IG-88A killed him and replaced his stormtrooper escorts with [[Stormtrooper droid|droid replicas]], but Jerjerrod preferred not having the supervisor there to complicate the already delicate matter of bringing the Death Star's construction back on schedule. As the stormtrooper droids unloaded the core, the Moff noted that they moved with near-mechanical precision and silently wished that all his men would be like them. However, when one of the stormtrooper droids was damaged by a falling cargo crane and activated its self-destruct, the resulting explosion took out an entire construction crew, much to Jerjerrod's chagrin.<ref name="Therefore I Am" />

The Emperor had become displeased with the slow progression of the Death Star project, and he sent the Supreme Commander, Darth Vader himself, to order the Moff to speed up the construction. Upon the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord's]] arrival aboard the incomplete Death Star, Jerjerrod made his way to the [[Hangar/Legends|hangar]] where [[ST 321/Legends|Vader's shuttle]] had landed,<ref name="ROTJ" /> waiting patiently at the bottom of the [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle/Legends|shuttle's]] ramp for Vader to disembark.<ref name="ROTJnovel">[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'' novel]]</ref> Vader was quick to inform Jerjerrod of the Palpatine's displeasure with the lack of progress in the battlestation's construction, brushing aside the Jerjerrod's concerns that the project was an impossible, under-crewed effort. When the Sith Lord revealed that his [[Sith Master/Legends|master]] was en route to personally oversee the final stage of construction, the Moff announced that his men would increase their work twofold.<ref name="ROTJ" /> Although Jerjerrod found conversations with Vader to have a certain quality of motivation, he had no intention of finding out if Vader was speaking the truth<ref name="CCG card" /> when the Emperor's [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] announced that he was more forgiving than the sovereign himself.<ref name="ROTJ" />

When the [[Emperor's personal shuttle/Legends|Emperor's shuttle]] landed aboard the Death Star, Vader and Jerjerrod were among the scores of Imperials present to greet Palpatine<ref name="ROTJ" /> in a brief ceremony limited to the docking bay.<ref name="ROTJ radio">{{RJRadio|Prophecies and Destinies}}</ref> When Palpatine and his cadre of advisors and [[Emperor's Royal Guard/Legends|Royal Guards]] disembarked, Vader informed him that the Death Star would be completed upon schedule. As they processed away from the shuttle, the Moff was one of the men to fall in line behind the two [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lords of the Sith]]. The Moff was later present in the [[Emperor's throne room#Death Star II|Emperor's throne room]] alongside the two Imperial leaders and [[Imperial Ruling Council/Legends|Imperial Ruling Council]] members [[Janus Greejatus/Legends|Janus Greejatus]] and [[Sim Aloo/Legends|Sim Aloo]],<ref name="ROTJ" /> whereupon Jerjerrod received confirmation that Palpatine's seat of power was acceptable.<ref name="ROTJ radio" /> At one point, Jerjerrod and two of Palpatine's Royal Guards attempted to bar Vader from entering the Emperor's throne room; the Sith Lord responded by [[Telekinesis/Legends|Force choking]] the Moff before sparing the man's life.<ref name="Character Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

====Battle of Endor and death====
{{Quote|Commander Jerjerrod, should the Rebels manage to blow up the shield generator, you will turn this battle station onto the Endor Moon and destroy it.''"<br />"''Yes, Your Highness, but we have several battalions stationed on&mdash;''"<br />"''You will destroy it!''"<br />"''Yes, Your Highness.|Palpatine and Jerjerrod during the Battle of Endor|<ref name="ROTJnovel" />}}
[[File:JerjerrodTheDestroyer-ROTJHD.jpg|thumb|right|250px|In the midst of the Battle of Endor, Jerjerrod was given the authority to fire the Death Star's superlaser at will.]]
The Emperor's arrival aboard the battlestation had been the final step of a carefully planned trap intended to destroy the Rebel Alliance. Following advice from [[Prince/Legends|Prince]] [[Xizor/Legends|Xizor]] of the [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] organization,<ref name="Shadows of the Empire">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (novel)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' novel]]</ref> Emperor Palpatine had deliberately allowed [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] [[Spy/Legends|spies]] to deliver the [[Death Star II plans|Death Star plans]] to the Alliance, knowing that the Rebel leadership would act upon the intelligence. With knowledge of the second Death Star's existence and the Emperor's presence aboard the station in hand, the Rebels took the bait and launched a two-phased attack on the construction site&mdash;as a [[Endor strike team/Legends|strike team]] traveled to the Endor moon to neutralize the [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|shield generator]] bunker, the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]] would emerge from [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] and send its [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] to destroy the Death Star's [[Hypermatter reactor/Legends|hypermatter reactor]]. Anticipating such a strategy, Palpatine had stationed his finest [[Legion/Legends|legion]] of [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] on Endor and gathered the bulk of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] on the far side of the moon, ready to spring the trap. When the Rebel [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] did arrive in the Endor system, it was caught between an Imperial armada and a [[Planetary shield/Legends|shielded]] Death Star. As the battle progressed, Palpatine opened a [[Comlink/Legends|channel]] to Jerjerrod in the [[Death Star command center|station's control room]] and ordered the latter to fire the Death Star's [[Concave Dish Composite Beam Superlaser|superlaser]] at will.<ref name="ROTJ" />

Though the assassin droid IG-88A had assumed nominal command of the [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]] upon the installation of his computer core,<ref name="Therefore I Am" /> the Imperials still maintained control over the station's prime weapon. Jerjerrod relayed the Palpatine's orders to a nearby [[Jad Bean/Legends|gunner]], and in short time, the prime weapon destroyed the [[Mon Calamari Star Cruiser/Legends|Mon Calamari Star Cruiser]] [[Liberty/Legends|''Liberty'']]. The realization that the Death Star was fully operational despite the ongoing construction stunned the Rebel fleet, as the Alliance vessels were unprepared to deal with the bigger threat posed by the station's superlaser. Nevertheless, the Alliance continued the fight, engaging the Star Destroyers on the outskirts of the battlefield in an attempt to buy more time for the strike team on Endor to accomplish its objective,<ref name="ROTJ" /> even as many more Rebel ships were destroyed by the battlestation's superlaser.<ref name="Therefore I Am" />

As the battle progressed, the Emperor gave the Moff one final order&mdash;should the [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|shield generator]] be neutralized, the Commander was to turn the Death Star on Endor and obliterate the moon. Though Palpatine did not share the Jerjerrod's concern for the Imperial troops present on the moon, the Moff acknowledged the command.<ref name="ROTJnovel" /> Ultimately, the Alliance strike team on Endor succeeded in destroying the generating station, bringing down the [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shield]] that protected the Death Star from a direct assault.<ref name="ROTJ" /> [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Endicott/Legends|Endicott]] brought word of the development to Commander Jerjerrod, adding that contact with the bunker on Endor had been lost. Recalling the Emperor's edict, the Moff reluctantly gave the order for the Death Star to fire on the moon, and the station began rotating to acquire its new target.<ref name="Blu-ray">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]''</ref>

[[File:FalconEscapesDSII-ROTJHD.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Jerjerrod perished when Alliance forces destroyed the Death Star.]]
With the shield down, [[General/Legends|General]] [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]], flying the [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|light freighter]] [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']], led several Rebel starfighters into the Death Star's superstructure while Rebel [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]] began firing on the station's hull. The bombardment thinned Jerjerrod's crew in the overbridge, with half of the personnel being killed, wounded, or simply frightened away. The remaining men were disorganized as chaos ensued in the control room, but the Moff made no effort to restore order. As an [[Aide/Legends|aide]] informed him that the Rebel fighters were eluding their defenses within the superstructure, a stunned Jerjerrod issued orders that made little sense, as his concentration had become focused solely on obliterating Endor. With the moon still out of range, he ordered the Death Star's rotation to be accelerated before being handed the superlaser's trigger by the fleeing aide. At sixty seconds left until firing, the Rebels had already taken out the main reactor; even as the station crumbled around him, Jerjerrod sat calmly and gazed out of the [[Viewscreen/Legends|viewscreen]]. When the countdown reached thirty seconds, the Death Star exploded,<ref name="ROTJnovel" /> killing the Moff<ref name="DB" /> before he could execute the Emperor's last command.<ref name="ROTJnovel" />

==Personality and traits==
[[File:Moff_Jerjerrod_2.jpg|thumb|right|250px|An unnerved Jerjerrod learns of Palpatine's impending visit.]]
{{Quote|Great men never hurried; great men caused ''others'' to hurry.|A fond saying of Jerjerrod's|<ref name="ROTJnovel" />}}
Tall and thin<ref name="ROTJnovel" />&mdash;he stood at a height of 1.7 [[Meter/Legends|meters]]<ref name="DB" /> and weighed 80 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]]<ref name="Chrome Perspectives" />&mdash;Jerjerrod had [[Color/Legends|brown]] [[Hair/Legends|hair]] and green [[Eye/Legends|eyes]].<ref name="ROTJ" /> He was a competent administrator, having been a desk general, but he possessed very little military experience.<ref name="GG5" /> He was arrogant and a self-described ambitious man,<ref name="ROTJnovel" /> though others, particularly his superiors, considered him to be quite the opposite,<ref name="TOSVC" /> believing him to lack creativity, motivation, and the audacity or vision to act on his ambition. Indeed, Palpatine saw him as only slightly ambitious, like any other Imperial officer. It was for these reasons that the Emperor assigned the Moff as the overseer of the Death Star's construction. Emperor Palpatine had no qualms about his selection; Commander Jerjerrod could get the Death Star finished in short time, but he would not mimic his predecessor, [[Governor/Legends|Governor]] Tarkin, and attempt to use the superweapon for his own personal gain.<ref name="GG5" />

Jerjerrod believed that great men such as himself never had any reason to hurry; rather, it was his job to cause other beings to hurry. But upon learning that the slow in the second Death Star's assembly had displeased the Emperor, and that he would be arriving to oversee the final stage of construction, the Moff reasoned that, on certain occasions, even great men hurried.<ref name="ROTJnovel" /> Jerjerrod did not know how he and his men could possibly complete the Death Star's construction on schedule, but he did not make excuses for their lack of progress&mdash;he had no intention of learning how Vader or Palpatine would respond to any such explanations.<ref name="Therefore I Am" />

[[File:MoffJerjerrod-SWI187.png|thumb|left|200px|The face of Jerjerrod]]
When ordered to destroy the Rebel fleet during the Battle of Endor, Jerjerrod became melancholic, for he had no wish to see the war end&mdash;ongoing war was one of his favorite things. However, he also loved the total annihilation of his enemy, and this gave him all the motivation he needed to order the gunners to fire the Death Star's superlaser. When the battle began turning in the Alliance's favor, Jerjerrod had time to reflect on the sudden turn of events. While his disorganized crew began to flee, the Moff simply sat and dwelt on his current situation, wondering how the Empire could possibly be on the brink of defeat. He could not believe that his patience, cleverness, and loyalty had not paid off, and his pride at commanding the second Death Star was no consolation. the Moff's hatred for the Rebellion had grown as the battle progressed; though he had once viewed the Alliance as something he could easily bully without fear of reprisal, it had matured and learned to fight back. Jerjerrod realized that the only act that could possibly satisfy him in such a despairing time was to fulfill the Palpatine's final order and destroy Endor, though he died before he could accomplish the feat.<ref name="ROTJnovel" />

==Equipment==
During his Imperial service, Moff Jerjerrod wore the standard [[Imperial officer's uniform/Legends|Imperial officer's uniform]].<ref name="ROTJ" /> He was armed with an [[E-11 blaster rifle/Legends|E-11 blaster rifle]].<ref name="Hasbro Toy" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Vaderchoke.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Vader Force-chokes Jerjerrod in a deleted scene from ''Return of the Jedi''.]]
Portrayed by [[Michael Pennington]], Moff Jerjerrod was created for [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], released on [[May 25]], [[1983]].<ref name="ROTJ" /> Actor [[Wikipedia:Alan Rickman|Alan Rickman]] had auditioned for the role, whom he wanted to play with a "Big, slow, low voice", but lost to Pennington.<ref name="Making">''[[The Making of Return of the Jedi]]''</ref> Though created for the film, the character of Jerjerrod first appeared in the [[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Return of the Jedi'' novelization]], published prior to the film's release.<ref name="ROTJnovel" /> Though his role in the film is relatively minor,<ref name="ROTJ" /> the novelization includes several additional scenes in which Jerjerrod is present,<ref name="ROTJnovel" /> many of which were shot but not included in the final version of the movie.<ref name="Blu-ray" /> As a result of a props "blooper" during production, Jerjerrod and all other Imperial officers wear the wrong [[Rank insignia plaque/Legends|rank badge]] in the film.<ref name="Insider 105">{{InsiderCite|105|25 Years of Return of the Jedi!|25 Years of ''Return of the Jedi''!}}</ref>

Addressed simply as "Commander" in the film, Jerjerrod's name is never heard during ''Return of the Jedi'', though his name is listed in the credits.<ref name="ROTJ" /> In the movie's [[1996]] [[Return of the Jedi (radio)|radio adaptation]], Jerjerrod was voiced by [[Peter Dennis]]. The radio adaptation was noteworthy for providing the pronunciation of "Jerjerrod."<ref name="ROTJ radio" /> Archival footage of Jerjerrod greeting Vader upon his arrival on the Death Star from ''Return of the Jedi'' was used for the [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|''Special Edition'']] release of [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''The Empire Strikes Back'']], though the scene itself is from a different angle. As a result, Jerjerrod is seen greeting Vader as he lands on the ''Executor'' following the duel on Bespin.<ref name="DB" /><ref name="ESB" /> In [[2009]], the Moff was given the first name "Tiaan" in ''[[The Essential Atlas]]''.<ref name="Atlas" />

The ''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]'', released in [[1989]], introduced an Admiral Jerjerrod that had served the Republic;<ref name="IS">''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]''</ref> this character was later established as being Moff Jerjerrod's grandfather in [[Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection 9|''The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection 9'']].<ref name="TOSVC" /> ''[[Coruscant and the Core Worlds]]'', released in [[2003]], mentioned the existence of a Jerjerrod family estate in [[Sirpar Hills]] on [[Anaxes/Legends|Anaxes]], but this has not been specifically tied to Moff Jerjerrod.<ref name="Coruscant">''[[Coruscant and the Core Worlds]]''</ref>

A slight inconsistency regarding Jerjerrod's height exists. While the [[StarWars.com]] [[Databank (original)|Databank]] indicated that Jerjerrod was 1.7 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in height,<ref name="DB" /> ''The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection 9'' supplies the slightly taller figure of 1.8 meters.<ref name="TOSVC" /> This article assumes that the former is correct.

===Script changes===
Over the course of ''Return of the Jedi''{{'s}} development, Jerjerrod's role expanded and contracted greatly. In earlier drafts, Jerjerrod&mdash;a Grand Moff described as a tall, confident technocrat&mdash;played a more prominent role as Palpatine's "secret agent," operating behind Vader's back while overseeing the transformation of the [[Endor/Legends|Green Moon]] of [[Had Abbadon]] into a paradise for the citizens of the overpopulated Imperial capital. While aboard Commander Jerjerrod's shuttle, Lord Vader informed him that he had sensed a Rebel presence on the moon, but the Grand Moff saw it as an insult to his work and refused to believe it&mdash;even as a stolen Imperial transport piloted by [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia]] and two other Rebels nearly collided with the shuttle. Upon arriving on Had Abbadon, Vader and Jerjerrod descended to the Emperor's throne room, which overlooked a lake of lava. Once Vader departed, having been reprimanded for not capturing Luke Skywalker, Palpatine tasked Jerjerrod with keeping an eye on Vader. Palpatine then explained that Skywalker would be replacing Vader, and that the Rebels were launching an attack on the Death Star. Jerjerrod later butted heads with one of Vader's generals, [[Maximilian Veers/Legends|Maximilian Veers]], who refused to take a captive Skywalker to Palpatine on Had Abbadon and instead delivered the prisoner to Vader on the ''Executor''. Furious, the Grand Moff stormed in on the Supreme Commander and demanded to know why the Jedi trainee was not delivered to the Emperor. In response, Vader grabbed Jerjerrod by the throat and killed him.<ref name="Annotated Screenplays">''[[Star Wars: The Annotated Screenplays]]''</ref>

In the revised rough draft, Jerjerrod's shuttle nearly intercepted Leia's captured transport when it moved to help a panicked [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]]&mdash;who was flying a captured [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE Fighter]] during the strike team's infiltration&mdash;without giving a clearance code. However, the situation was averted when Leia's craft was given clearance. Following the incident, Vader complained to Jerjerrod that Palpatine had not been in contact with him. Though Jerjerrod attempted to avoid an argument, he was forced to reveal that the Emperor, displeased with Vader's failure in capturing Luke Skywalker, had reassigned the Sith Lord to oversee the construction of the [[Habitation sphere|two new Death Stars]]. The Grand Moff explained that the Emperor doubted the Supreme Commander would be able to turn young Jedi to the dark side, a task only the Emperor could accomplish. Jerjerrod also revealed that Palpatinewas aware of the impending Rebel attack, and that Luke, who was on the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] at the time, would soon be in the hands of the Empire. Later, in the ''Executor''{{'s}} private communications chamber, Jerjerrod conversed with Palpatine's holographic form, which instructed him to deliver Skywalker to him behind Vader's back. The Grand Moff noted that the Rebel attack would be ample to distract the Supreme Commander from finding his son, allowing the Emperor to turn young captive to the dark side. Because Jerjerrod had used a coded transmission and had disabled all surveillance equipment, Vader had no knowledge of the conspiracy until after Skywalker was delivered to Palpatine. Upon learning of the secret dealings, the ireful Dark Lord of the Sith killed the Grand Moff.<ref name="Annotated Screenplays" />

===Deleted scenes===
[[File:ScrewYouStormies-ROTJBR.jpg|thumb|right|250px|In one of his deleted scenes, Jerjerrod reluctantly decides to turn the Death Star on Endor.]]
Even after the final version of the script was established, several of Jerjerrod's scenes were removed.<ref name="Insider 67">{{InsiderCite|67|The Ultimate Return of the Jedi Insider's Guide|The Ultimate ''Return of the Jedi'' Insider's Guide}}</ref><ref name="Blu-ray" /> In one of these, most likely intended as a bit of on-set humor, Jerjerrod is shocked by a Royal Guard with a [[Force pike/Legends|force pike]].<ref name="Insider 67" /> However, many of these deleted scenes were eventually released.<ref name="Blu-ray" /> In the first of these, filmed on [[February 18]], [[1982]], according to [[Star Wars Insider 24|''Star Wars Insider'' 24]]{{'s}} production timeline, Jerjerrod and two Royal Guards attempt to prevent Vader from seeing Palpatine; in response, the Dark Lord strangles the Moff using [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] but stops short of killing him.<ref name="Insider 67" /><ref name="Blu-ray" /> This scene was later referenced in the ''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> and included in the ''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]'' Blu-ray set.<ref name="Blu-ray" />

The Blu-ray set also included scenes from a subplot that involves the Moff's final orders.<ref name="Blu-ray" /> While largely present in the novelization, these scenes were ultimately cut from the film.<ref name="Ask Lobot">{{InsiderCite|106|Ask Lobot}}</ref> In these clips, the Emperor tasks Commander Jerjerrod with destroying Endor if the Rebels knock out the shield generator. Though he acknowledges the command, the Moff briefly expresses his concern for the Imperial troops still on the moon before the Emperor silences him. Later, as the battle begins to favor the Rebels, Lieutenant Endicott informs the Moff that the shield generator has been disabled, prompting Commander Jerjerrod to reluctantly prepare the station to fire on the Forest Moon. In the last of these clips, Jerjerrod issues several orders intended to impede the Rebel starfighters that have penetrated the Death Star's superstructure. Once the battlestation is in position to fire on Endor, Jerjerrod hesitates momentarily before giving the order to destroy the moon.<ref name="Blu-ray" />

===Non-canon biography===
The video game ''[[Star Wars: Demolition]]'' mentions that Jerjerrod and [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]] worked out a deal to move the latter's [[Jabba's demolition games|demolition games]] to the second Death Star. In ''[[The Return of Tag & Bink: Special Edition]]'', Jerjerrod appears as part of the Emperor's procession in the Death Star's docking bay, a scene inspired by the event as portrayed in ''Return of the Jedi''. In addition to Palpatine, Vader, Janus Greejatus, Sim Aloo and an Imperial officer, two [[Wikipedia:Cylon (1978)|Cylons]] from [[Wikipedia:Battlestar Galactica (1978 TV series)|''Battlestar Galactica'']] and [[Tag Greenly|Tag Greenley]] and [[Bink Otauna/Legends|Bink Otauna]], disguised as Royal Guards, are part of the procession. Jerjerrod also appears, as a [[LEGO Star Wars|LEGO]] minifigure, in the video games ''[[LEGO Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy]]'' and ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]''.

In [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']], Jerjerrod possesses good diplomatic and leadership skills, but his combat and espionage scores are negligible. Since the game starts after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] and follows a non-canon path of events, it is possible for Jerjerrod to survive the Galactic Civil War and witness the final defeat of the Rebellion.
